Louis Marchand (organist to the King of France)

The man who in 1717 agreed to a keyboard contest with Bach in Dresden, and fled on the morning of the day, has appeared at last. This time, he says, he will not run.
The real Marchand is said to have secretly listened to Bach play the night before, taken fright, and left Dresden by the early coach.
The English ballad opera The Beggar's Opera is sweeping London, mocking Italian opera as it goes. Can your orchestra win back the cheers of the public?
Diaghilev, the impresario from Russia, with Stravinsky, Nijinsky, Picasso and others at his side, has Paris and the world in a frenzy. Can your orchestra stand against the whirlwind of a new age?

Emperor Joseph II has ordered a best-of-three contest with the post of court Kapellmeister at stake. Salieri has every singer and player of the Viennese court behind him.
In real life, Salieri and Mozart wrote competing new works at the Emperor's command for Schönbrunn in 1786.
Opera buffa: Prima la musica e poi le parole
The Devil (the fiddler from the dream)

On a stormy night an unknown violinist appeared at the theatre: the very one, they say, who once came to Tartini in a dream and played the 'Devil's Trill'.

'Win, and eternal glory is yours. Lose… and I shall take one of your cities.'
Tartini said he composed the 'Devil's Trill' while trying to write down what the Devil had played in his dream.

The critic Hanslick marshals the Brahms party and delivers the last judgement in the name of 'the beautiful in music'.
Wagner is said to have modelled Beckmesser, the spiteful marker in Die Meistersinger, on Hanslick.
Wagner, with Ludwig II behind him, advances at the head of the whole army of his tetralogy. The 'music of the future', or the heir of Beethoven?
